Could you produce electricity by wrapping the levitating magnet area in some copper wire? Don't know if I'm remembering my physics correctly.

Nope. This isn't a perpetual motion device. If you put the levitating magnet inside of a copper coil it would eventually stop spinning, and get pulled out of position. Rather quickly, I imagine. This would be because of magnetic drag. Basically, whenever you induce an electric current in a wire you also create a magnetic field. The spinning magnet would induce an electric current in the wire, the wire would also become slightly magnetic. The magnetic field from the wire would interact with the magnetic field of the magnet, and create drag that would slow down the spin. Not to mention that it would throw the delicate balance out of whack, and cause the spinning magnet to get knocked out of place.
